title: Tabular and Graphical Representations for the Distributions of Two Categorical Variables
rights: Original teacher-authored public-safe practice; no private/secure assessments.

items.prompt: What does the App–Tea cell count of 2 represent?
items.hint: Read the row and column together.
items.solution: Two orders were placed using App and were Tea.
items.provenance: Maple Hill School original practice, November 2026

options.label: A
options.text: There were two App customers in total.

options.label: B
options.text: There were two drinks of any type.

options.label: C
options.text: Two App orders were for tea.

options.label: D
options.text: Two types of drinks were available.

items.prompt: Which is the correct App row margin?
items.solution: The App row contains 4 Coffee, 2 Tea, and 2 Smoothie orders; total 8.
items.provenance: Maple Hill School original practice, November 2026

items.prompt: Which comparison correctly describes Tea percentages by channel?
items.hint: Use each group's row total as denominator.
items.solution: Tea is 2/8=25% among App orders and 8/16=50% among Counter orders.
items.provenance: Maple Hill School original practice, November 2026

options.label: A
options.text: App 25%; Counter 50%.

options.label: B
options.text: App 2/24; Counter 8/24.

options.label: C
options.text: App 2/10; Counter 8/10.

options.label: D
options.text: App 50%; Counter 25%.

items.prompt: Both channels had 4 Coffee orders. What are their within-channel Coffee percentages?
items.solution: App Coffee=4/8=50%; Counter Coffee=4/16=25%. Equal counts need not yield equal percentages.
items.provenance: Maple Hill School original practice, November 2026

options.label: A
options.text: Both 50%.

options.label: B
options.text: Both 25%.

options.label: C
options.text: App 25%, Counter 50%.

options.label: D
options.text: App 50%, Counter 25%.

items.prompt: In a 100% segmented bar graph, why are App and Counter bars equally long?
items.hint: A complete bar represents a group.
items.solution: Each complete bar represents 100% of that group's observations, regardless of how many observations the group contains.
items.provenance: Maple Hill School original practice, November 2026

options.label: A
options.text: The raw counts are equal.

options.label: B
options.text: There must be no association.

options.label: C
options.text: Each bar represents the complete group, normalized to 100%.

options.label: D
options.text: The chart uses the grand total for every segment.

items.prompt: In a mosaic plot, what fraction of total area is the App–Tea cell?
items.hint: Multiply App group width by Tea height inside App.
items.solution: Area=(8/24)(2/8)=2/24=1/12; mosaic area represents joint relative frequency.
items.provenance: Maple Hill School original practice, November 2026

items.prompt: Which conclusion is supported by the observed café table?
items.solution: Tea is 25% of App orders and 50% of Counter orders, showing an association in these observations, not a causal effect.
items.provenance: Maple Hill School original practice, November 2026

options.label: A
options.text: The observed drink mixes differ by channel.

options.label: B
options.text: Choosing App causes preference for Coffee.

options.label: C
options.text: The drink mixes must be identical in all cafés.

options.label: D
options.text: Ordering channels were randomly assigned.

items.prompt: A different table has App 2,4,2 out of 8 and Counter 4,8,4 out of 16 for Coffee,Tea,Smoothie. What does that show?
items.hint: Compare each category divided by its own row total.
items.solution: Both channels have 25% Coffee, 50% Tea, 25% Smoothie, so there is no association in that constructed table.
items.provenance: Maple Hill School original practice, November 2026

options.label: A
options.text: Association because Counter counts are larger.

options.label: B
options.text: All drinks are equally likely.

options.label: C
options.text: No association because conditional proportions match.

options.label: D
options.text: The table must be an experiment.
